comments.author: scottschurr
comments.body:
With Flow now having a limit of 1000 (not 2000) offers at the same quality, I needed to adjust the CrossingLimits Offer Overflow test so it could demonstrate a case where:

- Taker stops consuming offers and returns `tesSUCCESS` while
- FlowCross attempts to consume too many offers and fails, returning `tecOVERSIZE`.

Here's a commit with the adjusted test: https://github.com/scottschurr/rippled/commit/8dfb7949aad455679d24d02f22ca1bfc1eac1fbe.  The test is not in good enough shape to be cherry-picked.  The final conditions need tuning based on how we decide to resolve the issue.

I'm not saying that the case demonstrated is important enough to deserve attention.  We could very well decide that we understand it and have decided not to worry about it.

The following commit addresses this specific failure mode: https://github.com/scottschurr/rippled/commit/e364ec9ce47820c73bee66b602bccde5abae2b52. There may be entirely too much plumbing associated with that commit considering the rarity of the problem.

prs.body:
This changes the rules for payments in two ways:

1) It sets the maximum number of offers any book step can consume from 2000 to
1000.

2) When a strand contains a step that consumes too many offers, currently the
liquidity is not used at all and the strand will be considered dry. This changes
things so the liquidity is used, however the strand will still be considered
dry.

prs.body:
First, only the (currently) top-most commit needs review.  Preceding commits are fixes that are in review and are prerequisites to the top-most commit.  They are: https://github.com/ripple/rippled/pull/2196, https://github.com/ripple/rippled/pull/2200, and https://github.com/ripple/rippled/pull/2202.  Presuming those three pull requests pass review this pull request is the next logical step.

In order to automatically run unit tests with newly created amendments, prefer to start with `jtx::supported_features()` and then subtract unwanted features.  This approach replaces most uses of `jtx::with_only_features()`, since that always excludes newly added features.

Some number of the modified tests did not pass with `featureFeeEscalation` enabled.  I "fixed" those tests by calling `env.close()` more often.  There may be a preferable solution.

These changes identified a few bugs that were hiding in amendment qualified code.  One of those bugs, in FlowCross, is not yet fixed.  By uncommenting the test in CrossingLimits_test.cpp you can see failures relating to that bug.  Since FlowCross is not yet enabled on the network we can fix the bug at our convenience.

As an aside, I noticed that there are a number of manual tests that seem to not be run on a regular basis.  I wonder if we could coerce one of our CI passes to run these tests?  If they ran in our coverage build that would be great, but it might make things too slow.  The manual tests include:

- CrossingLimits
- PlumpBook
- OversizeMeta
- FindOversizeCross
- PayStrandAllPairs
- hash_append
- hash_speed
- Timing
- NoRippleCheckLimits

All I know is that these are manual tests.  Not all of them may be appropriate for CI.

Reviewers: @seelabs, since many of the unit test I modified were his originally, @ximinez, to see if the FeeEscalation adjustments are correct.

reviewCommentsList.author: scottschurr
reviewCommentsList.body:
Tried this one.  In its current incarnation `addFeatures` doesn't behave well with a single `uint256`.  It really wants a collection.  I got the following to work, which is relatively low cost, but kind of wordy:
```
addFeatures(features, std::initializer_list<uint256 const>({featureTrustSetAuth}))
```
I ended up punting and using
```
features & ~with_only_features(featureTrustSetAuth)
```
on line 55.  I think that will be okay for now.
